comments.body: SCOPING NOTE. This epic's attestation went stale-head the moment the first child's commit landed (signed at b872bc3c8, HEAD e78c86be1). Cause: it was UNSCOPED — an epic with no file_impact dies on EVERY commit, which is the documented stale-head mode and would have recurred on every single child change through to the close. Setting file_impact now costs nothing because the attestation was ALREADY dead, and it makes the eventual close-time review durable: a scoped attestation only goes stale-code when one of ITS OWN dependency files drifts. The paths are the union of the four children's declared impacts. Sequencing that matters and burned a cycle earlier on this epic: do NOT edit this while a review of THIS ticket is in flight, and do not edit a CHILD's material while a review of this parent is in flight — that is what produced the stale-pin-drift that blocked the first sign attempt.

READY TO CLOSE, pending one fresh plan review. All four children are closed: b00f, d8ef, b300, b5fe.

EVERY MEASURED AC TARGET IS MET:
    src/rebar/llm/config.py                    631   (AC: at or below 640; was 793)
    src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py  511   (AC: at or below 560; was 794)
    src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py              243   (AC: at least 100, under 800)
    src/rebar/llm/plan_review/decide_ops.py    349   (AC: at least 100, under 800)
Plus: seam guards exist for both relieved files with per-file bounds; the full plan-review step-registry membership test exists and runs in a SUBPROCESS; every 'uses:' in gates/plan-review.yaml is asserted to resolve; gen_env_registry is clean AND complete after b00f registered _llm_float; and every relocation landed with ZERO edits to existing tests beyond the two mandated headroom tightenings.

WHY A FRESH REVIEW IS NEEDED, and it is a cost I chose knowingly: the signed attestation reads 'stale-head (UNSCOPED)'. It was signed BEFORE I set file_impact on this epic. Setting file_impact scopes FUTURE attestations; it does not retroactively scope one already signed. So the existing signature dies on every commit — which is precisely why I scoped the ticket mid-flight rather than leaving it. The next review will be scoped and will survive commits that do not touch its declared dependencies.

DELIBERATELY SERIALISED: not launching that review yet, because d23e's round-3 review is in flight and d23e is the critical path. The one time two plan reviews overlapped in this session, a review reported findings against ticket text that had already been superseded. Cheap to avoid by waiting.

WHAT THIS EPIC DID NOT DO, so the record is honest: it relieved the two files that were BLOCKING work and it did not drain the tier. plan_review/passes.py and _engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py both still sit at EXACTLY 800 with no ticket; attest.py is c6c9; signing.py is 798. And every cut here RELOCATED mass rather than dissolving an absorber — config.py's per-knob cost and decide's 213 lines are unchanged. The seam tests are the substitute ratchet for the per-function gate the operator declined.

# Preemptive hardening of low-headroom, high-centrality modules

## Context / Problem
ADR 0056 relieved `runner.py` — the single highest-churn file in the repo (27 commits per 400) —
from 689 to 647 LOC, giving it 153 lines of headroom. The treatment worked. It was never applied to
the next tier, and that tier is now blocking work.

MEASURED (churn per 400 commits / fan-in / LOC / headroom against the 800 cap in
`.github/module-size-limit.txt`):

  llm/config.py                 16 / 93 / 793 /  7   <- most central near-cap file in the repo
  llm/plan_review/passes.py     13 /  - / 800 /  0
  signing.py                     - / 42 / 798 /  2
  llm/plan_review/attest.py     21 / 38 / 800 /  0   (ticket c6c9)
  llm/plan_review/workflow_ops  16 /  - / 794 /  6
  _commands/transition_close    23 /  - / 793 /  7
  llm/plan_review/__init__.py   24 /  - / 768 / 32
  llm/runner.py                 27 / 68 / 647 / 153  <- ADR 0056; the proof the treatment works

SIX files sit within 7 lines of the cap. Three are at EXACTLY 800. This is already blocking:
ticket d23e's entire scope is `llm/config.py`, and a deprecation alias there costs 10-16 lines
against 7 available. MEASURED cost of one new config knob is 10-13 lines (`9ad46965bd` 34 lines/3
knobs, `1f63d74a03` 21/2, `75d1a4672d` 22/2, `434dc0a577` 26/2), so the headroom is less than ONE
knob.

## Approach
Relieve these files SEPARATELY and AHEAD of the work that must touch them, so no ticket discovers
the breach mid-flight the way d23e just did.

**The method is ADR 0056's, generalized: diagnose the SHAPE of the mass, then pick the matching
move.** The ADR proves this by declining to generalize ITSELF onto config.py (§Decision 5). Three
shapes observed:
 * ABSORBING VERB — one long method every feature edits. Move: extract verbs as plain functions with
   explicit parameters. (`runner.run()`, 59% of its file.)
 * FLAT DECLARATION TABLE — N near-identical per-field reads. Move: data-driven table.
 * COLOCATED DOMAINS — independent units merely sharing a file. Move: split on the domain seam.

**The test of any split, from the ADR: does it remove the thing that ABSORBS FUTURE CHANGE, or
merely relocate mass?** Extracting a callee always satisfies a per-FILE gate while the calling method
keeps absorbing — which is why runner.py regrew three times. Where a split only relocates mass, SAY
SO in the change rather than claiming permanence.

## The per-function ratchet is REJECTED — do not re-propose it
ADR 0056 §Decision 1 deferred a per-FUNCTION length gate and said "if the pattern recurs a fourth
time, the per-function gate is the answer". It was raised and the operator DECLINED it: blast radius
too high. MEASURED justification, from the ADR's own figures — 3,292 functions under `src/rebar`, 21
over 200 lines, 38 over 150, 62 over 120, 101 over 100, with the ten worst spanning six subsystems.
It would break six subsystems at once or require an allowlist, and epic 716f deliberately DRAINED
AND REMOVED the module-size allowlist.

CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this epic matters: the ratchet was the named remedy for ADR 0056's stated
residual risk ("nothing structurally prevents the decomposed run() from regrowing"). With it
declined, module-level rework plus SEAM TESTS are the only defence. The seam test is therefore
load-bearing, not decorative: change 1484 added `< 700` headroom assertions for `gate_dispatch.py`
and `orchestrator.py`, and those two are the comfortable files today BECAUSE of it. Every child here
ships a headroom guard for the file it relieves.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` -> a new `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` (child: unblocks d23e)
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` -> a new `plan_review/decide_ops.py`
- `scripts/gen_env_registry.py` (a found defect: `_llm_float` is invisible to the scanner)
- `tests/unit/` seam guards, including the two static checks that exist at NO layer today
- NOT in scope: `passes.py`, `attest.py` (c6c9), `signing.py`, `transition_close.py`. Recorded as
  known-remaining so the next reader is not misled into thinking this epic drains the tier.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC, and d23e can land its deprecation alias without any
      structural change of its own
- [ ] `llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` is at or below 560 LOC
- [ ] a seam test asserts a headroom target for EACH relieved file, and every new module clears the
      100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor AGENTS.md requires
- [ ] a test asserts the full expected plan-review step-registry membership — the guard that does not
      exist at any layer today, so a missed registration import currently cannot be caught statically
- [ ] a test asserts every `uses:` in `gates/plan-review.yaml` resolves in `STEP_REGISTRY`
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check` is clean AND complete, i.e. no env var read
      through a helper is missing from `docs/env-vars.md`
- [ ] every relocation lands with ZERO edits to existing tests; a required test edit means the cut is
      wrong and is the revert signal
